paper.title_en: Suppression of heavy-ion fusion by slow quasifission
paper.abstract_en:
Background: The fusion of heavy nuclei can be conceptually divided into two steps: capture of the projectile and target, then evolution towards a compact fully equilibrated compound nucleus. Reseparation through quasifission after capture inhibits compound nucleus formation, leading to fusion suppression.
Purpose: We aim to determine quantitatively the correlation between the degree of fusion suppression resulting from quasifission and the observed characteristics of the quasifission events themselves.
Method: Evaporation residues were measured for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Si</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>28</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Os</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>192</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>34</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>186</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> forming the compound nucleus <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Th</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>220</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, and identified using the implantation-decay method. Fusion suppression factors for these reactions (and others from the literature also forming <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Th</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>220</mn></mmultiscripts></math>) were determined relative to the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Pb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>204</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction. Fission characteristics were also measured for these three reactions, as well as for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>48</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>172</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>.
Results: Overall, fusion probabilities are found to fall rapidly as the charge product <math><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> increases above the value for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Pb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>204</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>. Crucially, although significant suppression of the <math><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> evaporation residue yield is observed for the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Si</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>28</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>34</mn></mmultiscripts></math> reactions, there is no significant fission mass-angle correlation that would signal the presence of fast quasifission. However, fission mass widths are larger than those expected based on the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Pb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>204</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> mass widths, taken as corresponding to fusion-fission.
Conclusions: Formation of an equilibrated compact compound nucleus can be suppressed by over 50% due to (slow) quasifission, even when no significant evidence of a mass-angle correlation is seen. Evidence of slow quasifission is shown by the increased mass widths observed.
